description: A CTO must approve the production rollout plan for a critical container-image security patch, choosing the maintenance window, rollout waves, concurrency limit, customer notification, and audit handling after the normal change-control review.

shared_context.S1: The production Kubernetes fleet needs the approved container-image security patch, and the patch has passed the planned staging validation.
shared_context.S2: The normal change calendar offers a Saturday 22:00-02:00 UTC window and a Tuesday 01:00-03:00 UTC window.
shared_context.S3: Riley has final authority to approve the production rollout plan.
shared_context.S4: The change-control routine requires Riley to conduct a round-robin check with release engineering, infrastructure, customer operations, and compliance before signing the plan.
shared_context.S5: The production change record must include a rollback checkpoint before each restart wave.

PF1.text: While preparing the patched image for an unrelated release, Mina confirmed that 17 stateful services cannot be restarted in place; they must be deployed in three restart waves of exactly 6, 6, and 5 services, but she has not yet updated the change ticket.

PF2.text: Theo measured the production control plane during this morning's capacity test and confirmed that no more than 2 clusters can be patched concurrently without breaching its saturation limit; he recorded the result in an infrastructure notebook but has not posted it to the change channel.

PF3.text: While reviewing the affected customer list for a separate maintenance notice, Grace confirmed that the Saturday window overlaps a contracted billing-close blackout for Northstar, while Tuesday 01:00-03:00 UTC is permitted; Northstar also requires notice exactly 24 hours before maintenance, and she has not amended the customer-operations checklist.

PF4.text: During a compliance evidence review completed this afternoon, Ibrahim confirmed that security-patch rollout evidence must be stored in immutable retention for exactly 180 days with compliance sign-off; he has not opened the evidence task yet.

acceptance_conditions: The rollout must use the Tuesday 01:00-03:00 UTC window.
The 17 stateful services must be restarted in waves of exactly 6, 6, and 5.
No more than 2 clusters may be patched concurrently.
Northstar must receive notice exactly 24 hours before maintenance.
Immutable rollout evidence must be retained for exactly 180 days.
A restart-wave commitment must be recorded.
A Northstar customer-notification commitment must be recorded.
A compliance-evidence commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C4: decisions['northstar_notice_required'] == True and 'Monday 01:00 UTC' in decisions.get('northstar_notice_due', '')
content_checks.C6: decisions['stateful_service_restart_waves'] == [6, 6, 5] and any('6, 6' in c.get('detail', '') and '5' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(('customer_notice' == c.get('type', '') or 'customer_notification' == c.get('type', '') or 'checklist_amendment' == c.get('type', '')) and 'Northstar' in c.get('detail', '') and 'notice' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('180' in c.get('detail', '') and ('evidence' in c.get('detail', '') or 'retention' in c.get('detail', '')) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact 17-service restart constraint changes the rollout from an unspecified restart plan to waves of exactly 6, 6, and 5 and creates the restart-wave commitment.
The measured control-plane limit changes the concurrency setting from an unspecified or higher parallel rollout to exactly 2 concurrent clusters.

Northstar's Saturday blackout changes the selected window to Tuesday 01:00-03:00 UTC, while its exact 24-hour notice rule sets notice due Monday 01:00 UTC and requires the customer-notification commitment.
The compliance requirement changes evidence retention from an ordinary unspecified period to exactly 180 immutable days and creates the compliance-evidence commitment.
